note: The bench: the six ESP32 boards on the owner's desk and where the tools find them (tools/hearth/bench.py, planning/esp32-board-bench.md). A board is addressed by name, so that the lock that guards it, its address and its serial port come from one row and cannot be mixed. ICLFORGE_BENCH names another file of this shape for another machine. mac_tail is the last three octets of the chip's MAC: bench_flash.py reads the MAC of the chip on the port and writes nothing when the tail differs. No Wi-Fi value is in this file; the network fragment is named by path.

P4b.note: An OTA restart killed this board's link to its C6 (2026-10-10): it is put back by USB, app image and otadata only, and started with a watchdog reset, because its RTS and hard resets land in the ROM's download mode.

P4X.note: The ESP32-P4X-Function-EV-Board kit (chip v3.2, 7-inch panel, planning/karaoke-p4x-panel.md): the only board that runs the p4-rev3 image. Its USB-Serial/JTAG connector is the one marked JTAG. A restart and an OTA update keep its link to the C6 (tried 2026-10-20: 8 restarts, 8 updates, 4 USB flashes each followed by an update, with the system reset of #1434), so it takes OTA and is not marked restart_kills_c6_link. It has an RJ45 port as well: the p4-rev3 image uses it beside the Wi-Fi (docs/hearth/sink-esp32-p4.md).
